concepts.def: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd

walkthroughs.body_html:
The SI system rests on 7 base units:

- metre (m) — length
- kilogram (kg) — mass
- second (s) — time
- ampere (A) — current
- kelvin (K) — temperature
- mole (mol) — amount
- candela (cd) — luminous intensity

Redefined 2019: each tied to a fundamental constant (e.g. kg via Planck's h).

From base units we build others:

- Force: N = kg m s⁻².
- Energy: J = N m = kg m² s⁻².
- Power: W = J/s = kg m² s⁻³.
- Pressure: Pa = N/m² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².
- Electric potential: V = J/C = kg m² s⁻³ A⁻¹.

Coherent: no conversion factors needed.

Standard SI prefixes:

- pico (p) 10⁻¹², nano (n) 10⁻⁹, micro (μ) 10⁻⁶, milli (m) 10⁻³.
- kilo (k) 10³, mega (M) 10⁶, giga (G) 10⁹, tera (T) 10¹².

1 GW (power station) = 10⁹ W; 1 nm (atom) = 10⁻⁹ m.

Dimensional analysis: check each side has same units to validate equations.
